scope: Direct decoded authoritative project files and exact generator/proposal; no audio perception. Full render evidence pending, acceptance and owner listening separate. All scores are provisional source-based musical judgments, not measurements.

prior_dispositions.chord_quality: implemented before Round1 including Fm sparse bass third
prior_dispositions.bass_register: implemented before Round1 at 9a2d099; all bass events down 12 semitones

issues.R1-A: Articulation: bass gates remain 4–12 raw ticks, intentionally staccato per the revised proposal. At 96 PPQN these do not supply the earlier promised held roots. Keep short pickups but lengthen selected foundations and lead endpoints; judge the resulting envelope on render. The octave correction is accepted.
issues.R1-B: Development: scenes 1 and 5, and scenes 3 and 6, are event-and-lock identical within every song. Repeated chain entries are also identical. Compose later-section differences and meaningful last-pass endings.
issues.R1-C: Transitions: lock shapes reset each bar, builds retain late bass notes, bridges retain kicks, and endings reuse the progression. Write progressive builds, subtractive contrasts, pickups and closing cadences.
issues.R1-D: Harmony: chord quality now matches labels, but all chord stacks use root position and restart the same four-chord sequence each scene. Use common tones/inversions, selective top-note movement and contrasting bridge harmonic rhythm.
issues.R1-E: Melody/groove: motives have identifiable contours and genre kick grids, but lead gates are uniformly short, track7 often overlaps rather than answering and its claimed fifth lift is not implemented. Shape rests, held endpoints and complementary response placement.
issues.R1-F: Lunar identity: useful inherited filter LFO and retriggered chord timbre envelope exist, plus two lock lanes. Develop one musically recognisable modulation gesture per song tied to an arrangement event; more modules alone would not improve score.
issues.R1-G: Future-bass arp: Up-Down 1/8 over two octaves with 34-tick peak chord gates and Latch Off needs deliberate redesign or rendered validation against the promised broad swells; first gate is shorter than the 48-tick arp interval.
issues.R1-H: Space/novelty: titles and common hall are insufficient. Make Afterglow drift, Event Horizon suspension/release, Packet Bloom transmission interruption, and Neon Transit recurring pulse distinct through phrase/routing/modulation design. Novelty means differentiation within these four original demos, not a verified world-first claim.

scenes.name: Intro
scenes.fix: Let the intro establish the drifting chord colour before the full bass/lead answer: withhold track 7 for two bars, sustain a low A root, and introduce the hat in bar 3. Give the last intro bar a melodic pickup into Verse.

scenes.name: Verse
scenes.fix: Keep the kick/backbeat and six-note identity, but lengthen selected root gates into patient phrases, retain the corrected low bass register, and voice-lead the chord tops. Add a two-bar answer that rests when the lead speaks.

scenes.name: Lift
scenes.fix: Make Lift grow across its four bars, rather than restart the same four-point locks every bar. Increase brightness or chord register progressively, then remove the final bass attack so Hook has an arrival.

scenes.name: Hook
scenes.fix: Preserve the A–C–E opening and D–C–B answer; develop an eight-bar sentence with one held ending and a cadential return to A. The existing short gates and four-bar shifts do not create the promised long warm hook.

scenes.name: Bridge
scenes.fix: Create a real eight-bar release: retain harmony and one distant reply, remove the kick for at least a phrase, thin or silence bass, then reintroduce one element to lead into Vrs2. Current chord stabs are denser than Verse.

scenes.name: Vrs2
scenes.fix: Compose a second verse from the hook fragments: exchange lead and response roles for bars 1–4, then return a lower register phrase. Change at least the last two bars to prepare Hook2; it is currently identical to Verse.

scenes.name: Hook2
scenes.fix: Create the promised final lift through a new top voice or counterline in bars 5–8 and a different bass pickup, while preserving the primary hook. Thin the penultimate bar before its final statement.

scenes.name: Outro
scenes.fix: Write a closing cadence instead of recycling the hook tail over all four chords. Remove kick then hats across the four bars, resolve lead to A over an Am ending, and leave a deliberate tail before Stop.

scenes.name: Intro
scenes.fix: Introduce the half-time backbeat identity sooner and begin with sustained low F/Db foundations. The current edge snare at step 12 implies a different backbeat from the rest of the song; use that displacement deliberately or change it.

scenes.name: Verse
scenes.fix: Anchor the half-time snare with the corrected low bass voice, selective sustained roots and gaps before its attack. Establish a recognisable short pickup that can expand in Drop rather than leaving all parts similarly clipped.

scenes.name: Build
scenes.fix: Build a four-bar tension trajectory: increasingly close drum subdivisions, rising chord colour, and final half-beat withdrawal of kick/bass. Current last bass event at step 14 and identical per-bar lock resets contradict the stated build.

scenes.name: Drop
scenes.fix: Resolve the chord-engine choice: the eighth-note Up-Down arp with 34-tick chord gates cannot be assumed to produce wide sustained chord swells. Hold chord triggers long enough or disable arp for the block swell; give the hook a two-phrase response and alter the fourth repeat ending.

scenes.name: Break
scenes.fix: Make Break a register and density reset. Suspend drums/bass for a phrase, expose the FM reply or sustained harmony, and use its final bar to rebuild the verse pulse.

scenes.name: Vrs2
scenes.fix: Derive a variation with changed bass rhythm and an answering upper line, preserving the first verse identity. Vrs2 presently copies all verse events and locks; distinguish its last bar to lead into Drop2.

scenes.name: Drop2
scenes.fix: Give Drop2 the promised changed bass and upper answer, then vary successive eight-bar passes through staged layer exits/entries or alternate ending scenes. Thirty-two bars repeating the identical scene after an identical earlier 32-bar drop is the main pacing failure.

scenes.name: Outro
scenes.fix: Close on a deliberate F-minor resolution with diminishing rhythmic activity and a planned effect tail. Current four-bar edge formula returns to the same harmony cycle and leaves a weakly prepared Stop.

scenes.name: Build
scenes.fix: Increase density or pitch tension over four bars and remove the last bass/kick pulse. Add the promised pitch/decay gesture at the phrase boundary; repeated brightness/timbre pulses alone do not make a build.

scenes.name: Bloom
scenes.fix: Keep the offbeat hat lattice and large motif leaps, but give the high A5 an answering lower phrase and occasional longer resolution. Differentiate the second/third eight-bar passes with a displaced fill or selective dropout, not only identical loop relaunches.

scenes.name: Glitch
scenes.fix: Make Glitch a composed interruption: use a short silence, one displaced drum fragment, and a contrasting pluck register or pitch/decay lock, then explicitly restore the pulse. The present two-kick bar with ordinary hats does not deliver the promised edit.

scenes.name: B-side
scenes.fix: Flip the call/response register and onset relationship as proposed; retain the motif contour but exchange high and low statements across the two phrases. B-side currently duplicates A-side exactly.

scenes.name: Bloom2
scenes.fix: Write the promised second-bloom register exchange plus a changed final cadence. Preserve the main rhythmic fingerprint while reserving a unique last-pass gesture; it currently duplicates Bloom.

scenes.name: Outro
